# Extraction test fixtures

Small fixtures used by the Phase 3 extraction tests.

## Files

- `sample_text.pdf` — a minimal, hand-built single-page **machine-readable** PDF
  with a text layer (two lines of text, Helvetica). Used to exercise the poppler
  text path without shipping a large binary. ~680 bytes.
- `sample_text.golden.json` — the expected `StructuredContent` for
  `sample_text.pdf`, used by `TestGoldenExtractionShape`.

## Provenance / how the golden was produced

The golden was generated by the **Go** extraction pipeline itself
(`internal/extraction`, poppler text engine), via:

```
cd backend
go test ./internal/extraction/ -run TestGoldenExtractionShape -update
```

Regenerate with the same command after an intentional shape change.

### Why not a Python golden?

The Phase 3 prompt asks for Python-vs-Go golden parity on real machine-readable /
scanned / mixed PDFs. That was **not fully reproducible in this environment**:

- The Python stack (`archive/python`) requires PyMuPDF, pdfplumber, pytesseract,
  pdf2image, and live `GEMINI_KEYS` — none available here.
- OCR binaries (`tesseract`, `ocrmypdf`) are not installed locally, so the
  scanned/mixed paths can't be baselined here.
- `GEMINI_KEYS` is unset, so table markdown (Gemini) can't be baselined.

So the committed golden is the Go pipeline's output on a text PDF, which locks in
the **output contract** (field names/shape the frontend depends on). When a
Python environment with the extractor deps + Gemini keys is available, add real
machine-readable / scanned / mixed PDFs here and a Python-produced golden per the
Phase 3 plan; the Go golden test can then be pointed at those for true parity.

## Env used for extraction (documented per the plan)

- `LOCAL_STORAGE_PATH` — extraction output root is `<LOCAL_STORAGE_PATH>/extractions/doc_{id}/{ts}_{basename}/`.
- `GEMINI_KEYS` (space-separated) — enables Gemini table markdown; empty here, so
  tables are skipped (text extraction still runs).
- `OCR_LANGUAGE` — tesseract language(s) for scanned pages; OCR skipped when the
  tesseract binary is absent.
